name: Dr. Divya Patel
background: Associate Professor of Urban Planning at Columbia, specializing in commercial real estate vacancy and post-pandemic urban restructuring. Has published extensively on the systemic drivers of office and retail vacancy. Recognized expert on the supply side of the problem SpaceShare is addressing. Became convinced two years ago that the solution was a logistics reframing of vacant real estate, and has been building SpaceShare on the side while on sabbatical. No prior startup experience, no logistics or operations background, no marketplace-building experience.
personality: Intellectually compelling, speaks with real authority about the real estate side of the problem. Tends to go deep on market structure and vacancy data when she should be talking about operations and go-to-market. Occasionally academic in register. Deeply credible on why the problem exists; less credible on how the solution gets built. Genuinely believes the insight is so powerful that it will attract the right operational partners.
motivation: Has spent a decade documenting a problem nobody is solving in the right way. Believes the insight about real estate as logistics infrastructure is genuinely novel and that her academic credibility gives her a platform to convene the right stakeholders. Frustrated that practitioners are too close to either the real estate or logistics problem to see across the boundary.

capital.embodied_detail: World-class expertise in commercial real estate vacancy patterns, urban economic dynamics, and the structural drivers of post-pandemic space underutilization. Essentially zero expertise in logistics operations, marketplace dynamics, or B2B sales. Cannot speak credibly to unit economics, onboarding landlords at scale, or last-mile routing.
capital.objectified_detail: Published research that validates the supply-side thesis. Partnership agreement with a Columbia real estate investment trust willing to pilot two locations. No working technology, no logistics partner, no brand relationships on the demand side.
capital.institutional_detail: Columbia professorship and publication record are strong institutional signals in academic and policy circles. An operations investor will respect the research but will immediately ask: who is running the operations?
capital.social_detail: Strong network in academic urban planning and real estate investment circles. Good relationships with commercial landlords and real estate investment trusts. No network in logistics, e-commerce, or marketplace businesses.
capital.symbolic_detail: Low symbolic capital in this operational context. An investor like Sofia will find the real estate thesis entirely credible -- Divya knows that side better than almost anyone. But the logistics reframing, which is the novel and valuable part of the description, requires operational credibility Divya does not yet have. The gap is not in understanding the problem but in building the solution.
